public_rationale: Anthropic tested withholding Claude Code from some new Pro subscribers while preserving access for existing subscribers. That contradicts the categorical claim that existing customers always bear restrictions first. It does not establish that revenue pressure never causes restrictions or that existing customers generally receive favorable treatment.
limitations: The counterexample was a small, temporary experiment at Anthropic.
The evidence refutes the universal allocation claim without resolving the broader causal theory.

statement.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic need to show continued revenue growth, which means that they must have capacity available for new customers, which means that old customers will always be the first to be punished.

our_interpretation: Punishment means reduced access, tighter usage limits, or removal of an included service.
First compares existing customers with new customers. It does not compare cheaper and more expensive subscription tiers.
Always is a categorical commitment. A documented allocation decision that protects existing subscribers while restricting new subscribers can contradict it.
The revenue-growth premise is part of the proposed causal explanation, not a separate conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: Allocation policies and decisions at both companies establish that preserving capacity for revenue growth consistently makes existing customers bear restrictions before new customers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Either company restricts access for new subscribers while preserving the corresponding access for existing subscribers in a decision addressing demand or subscription capacity.
